title: B185 — Free time tracking per Linear issue (ActivityWatch + Linear-derived cycle time)
description:
The lab has no time tracking. Found in the B119 Linear integrations walk (2026-09-25): **Rize** (the directory's time tracker) is paid, and [**Reclaim.ai**](<http://Reclaim.ai>)'s Linear integration is paid-only. Free options were compared:

| Option | How it captures time | Linear link | $0 | Fit |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **Clockify** | manual start/stop timer — a button on each Linear issue via the browser extension | **yes** — Linear is on Clockify's integrations list; free plan includes the extension | free forever | closest free equivalent of Rize/Toggl; cloud (fine — it's free) |
| **ActivityWatch** | **automatic** — runs on rogueone, records active window + Chrome tab title | **indirect** — a Linear tab title carries the issue ID (`EMA-241 …`), so time per issue is derivable | free, open source, local | lab-native: zero clicks, data stays local, could feed Grafana |
| **Linear's own timestamps** | nothing to run — each issue's status history (started/completed) is in the API | native | free | elapsed time per issue, **not** hours worked |
| Toggl Track | manual timer extension | **no** — Linear is not on its supported-app list | free tier | worse than Clockify here |
| Harvest | manual timer; time entries per Linear issue (a Linear-directory integration, seen 2026-09-26) | **yes** | reportedly 1 seat / 2 projects free | another manual-timer option beside Clockify |
| Timely | **automatic** AI time tracking with a Linear integration (seen 2026-09-26) | yes | paid | the only automatic tracker in the directory besides ActivityWatch — but not free |
| Everhour / TrackingTime / TMetric | timers on Linear issues (Linear-directory integrations, seen 2026-09-26; Everhour adds estimates + budgets) | yes | unverified | more manual-timer options — same category as Clockify |
| Traqq | manual start/stop timer from Linear issues (browser extension; a Linear-directory integration, seen 2026-09-26); Linux desktop app; does **not** auto-track app/URL use | **yes** (appears on free) | free: 3 users, **1 project** | manual timer — same category as Clockify, with a tighter project cap |
| solidtime / Kimai | self-hosted timers | not confirmed (solidtime has only a discussion thread) | free, open source | a service to run for no gain over Clockify |

**Recommendation:** skip timer apps — a solo operator switching between issues rarely starts/stops a timer consistently. Use **ActivityWatch** (automatic, local) for hours-per-issue, derived from Linear issue IDs in tab titles, plus **Linear-derived cycle time** (status history via the API — `check-linear-sync.sh` already queries it) for time-to-done. **Clockify** is the fallback if an explicit per-issue button is wanted.

**Scope**

1. Install ActivityWatch on rogueone (+ its browser watcher); confirm Linear tab titles carry the issue ID.
2. A small report: hours per EMA/B issue from ActivityWatch, and cycle time from Linear status history.
3. Decide where it surfaces (Grafana panel? Port? a weekly note) and whether it stays local-only.
4. DoD: runbook, demo, the host install tracked (B180), docs.

Relates B119, B180 (host installs). Detail: [https://github.com/edtbl76/weyland-lab/blob/main/docs/backlog.md](<https://github.com/edtbl76/weyland-lab/blob/main/docs/backlog.md>)
